module.dns_records.checks: Reads the domain's A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, SOA, CNAME and CAA records, detects a non-existent domain (NXDOMAIN) and wildcard answers.
module.dns_records.fix:
Open the domain's DNS zone at your DNS host or registrar and compare each record found (A, AAAA, MX, NS, TXT, CNAME, CAA) with what you have actually deployed: any record whose purpose nobody knows must be documented or deleted.
Delete the A, AAAA and CNAME records that point to a server or service you no longer use: an abandoned name can be taken over by a third party or lead to a machine you no longer control.
Check that the name servers (NS) are those of your current DNS host, identical in the zone and at the registrar, and that there are at least two of them, on different networks.
Check the MX records: each name must point to an existing mail server. If the domain never receives mail, publish a null MX (`0 .`) to declare it.
If the scan reports that the domain does not exist (NXDOMAIN) although it should be live: check at the registrar that it has not expired, that its name servers are filled in, and that the zone is loaded at the DNS host.
Complete the zone with the missing protections: a CAA record (module "Additional DNS records (CAA, SRV, TLSA)"), then SPF, DKIM and DMARC if the domain sends mail (mail modules).
Check the result with the commands in the snippet, wait for the TTL (validity period) of the old record to pass, then run the scan again.
module.dns_records.fix_snippet:
# DNS
example.com.        3600 IN NS    ns1.example.net.
example.com.        3600 IN NS    ns2.example.net.
example.com.        3600 IN A     203.0.113.10
example.com.        3600 IN AAAA  2001:db8::1
example.com.        3600 IN MX    10 mail.example.com.
www.example.com.    3600 IN CNAME example.com.

# Bash
dig +short NS example.com
dig +short A example.com
dig +short AAAA example.com
dig +short MX example.com
dig +short TXT example.com
dig +short CAA example.com
module.dns_records.title: DNS records
module.dns_records.why: DNS is the technical identity card of the domain: hosting, mail, allowed certificate authorities. A forgotten or inconsistent record opens the door to hijacking.
